hints.content:
The basic function $\cos(x)$ has a maximum point at $(0,1)$ and intersects its midline at $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2},0\right)$.

$\qquad$[[☃ image 1]]

Let's transform $\pink{\cos(x)}$ to $\blue{0.5\cos\left(\dfrac{1}{3}x+\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)-2}$ step by step and see how the graph changes along the way.

options.alt: A trigonometric wave on a x y coordinate plane. The y-axis scales by one. The x-axis scales by pi over two. The wave travels up to one on the y-axis at the point (zero, one) and down to negative one on the y-axis intersecting the midline at the point (pi over two, zero). The wave is at one on the y-axis at negative four pi, negative two pi, zero, two pi, and four pi. It is at negative one on the y-axis at negative five pi, negative three pi, negative pi, pi, three pi, and five pi.

hints.content:
The transformation from $\pink{\cos(x)}$ to $\green{\cos\left(\dfrac{1}{3}x\right)}$ is a horizontal stretch by a factor of $\dfrac{1}{\frac{1}{3}}=3$, so the intersection point's horizontal distance from the origin is stretched from $0.5\pi$ to $1.5\pi$.

$\qquad$[[☃ image 1]]

The transformation from $\green{\cos\left(\dfrac{1}{3}x\right)}$ to $\red{0.5\cos\left(\dfrac{1}{3}x\right)}$ is a vertical shrink by a factor of $2$, so the maximum point's vertical distance from the origin is shrunk from $1$ to $0.5$.

$\qquad$[[☃ image 2]]

options.alt: Two waves on a x y coordinate plane. The y-axis scales by one. The x-axis scales by pi over two. One wave is a dotted line while the other wave is a solid line. The waves both travel up to one on the y-axis and down to negative one on the y-axis. The dotted wave is at one on the y-axis at the point (zero, one), negative four pi, negative two pi, two pi, and four pi. It intersects the midline at the point (pi over two, zero). It is at negative one on the y-axis at negative five pi, negative three pi, negative pi, pi, three pi, and five pi. The solid wave touches one on the y-axis at zero. It intersects the midline at (three pi over two, zero) It touches negative one on the y-axis at negative three pi and three pi.

Two waves on a x y coordinate plane. The y-axis scales by one. The x-axis scales by pi over two. One wave is a dotted line while the other wave is a solid line. The dotted wave travels up to one on the y-axis and down to negative one on the y-axis. The solid wave travels up to one half on the y-axis and down to negative one half on the y-axis. The dotted wave is at one on the y-axis at the point (zero, one), negative four pi, negative two pi, two pi, and four pi. It is at negative one on the y-axis at negative five pi, negative three pi, negative pi, pi, three pi, and five pi. The solid wave touches one half on the y-axis at zero. It intersects the midline at the point (three pi over two, zero). It touches negative one half on the y-axis at negative three pi and three pi.

hints.content: The transformation from $\red{0.5\cos\left(\dfrac{1}{3}x\right)}$ to $\blue{0.5\cos\left(\dfrac{1}{3}x+\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)-2}$, which is equivalent to $0.5\cos\left(\dfrac{1}{3}(x+2\pi)\right)-2$, is a translation to the left by $2\pi$ units and a translation downwards by $2$ units.

As a result of these transformations, the maximum point is now at $\left(-2\pi,-1.5\right)$ and the intersection with the midline is at $(-0.5\pi,-2)$.

The resulting graph looks as follows:

$\qquad$[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A trigonometric wave on a x y coordinate plane. The y-axis scales by one. The x-axis scales by pi over two. The wave travels up to negative one and one half on the y-axis at the point (negative two pi, negative one and one half) and down to negative two and one half on the y-axis intersecting the midline at the point (negative pi over two, negative two). The wave is at negative one and one half on the y-axis at negative two pi and four pi.
